findings.finding: Insights: From “sum double” and “product quadruple” get a+A=2(b+B) and aA=4bB. Transfer 5 sweets makes sums equal → a+A = b+B+10, giving b+B=10 and a+A=20. Thus A=20‑a, B=10‑b. Remaining conditions: a(20‑a)=4b(10‑b) and a(15‑a)=b(15‑b). Brute‑force a∈[1,15], b∈[1,10] (A≥5) yields only (a,b)=(10,5). Product of ages = 10·5 = {answer = 50}.

Insights: From sums: A+a=2(B+b) and A+a=B+b+10 ⇒ B+b=10, A+a=20. Let a=20−A, b=10−B (≥0, a≥5 ⇒ A≤15). Product equations give A(20−A)=4B(10−B) and A(15−A)=B(15−B). Brute‑force A∈[1,15], B∈[1,10] → only (A,B)=(10,5). Product of ages =10·5=50. Pitfalls: ensure sweets non‑negative and a≥5; ages positive.
